title: Motor execution dataset from Wairagkar et al 2018
description: EEG recordings from 14 healthy, BCI-naive participants performing asynchronous voluntary index-finger tapping (right, left) and rest, originally reported by Wairagkar et al. (2018). Data were recorded at 1024 Hz from 19 scalp channels and preprocessed with filtering and ICA artifact removal. Trials are segmented around movement onset to study neural correlates of movement intention, and the dataset is distributed in BIDS format via MOABB.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a Deymed TruScan 32 amplifier using 19 Ag/AgCl ring electrodes (10-20 layout, reference FCz, ground AFz) at 1024 Hz. Participants tapped their index finger at a self-chosen time within a 10-second window after a visual text cue. Preprocessing included DC offset removal, 0.5 Hz high-pass, 50 Hz notch and 60 Hz low-pass filtering, EEGLAB infomax ICA artifact removal, and segmentation from -3 to +3 s around movement onset.
